text:
Lina M: quick weirdness — median for /v1/generate dropped ~30ms vs yesterday but p95/p99 look identical. dashboard median is LOWER than most endpoint-specific medians, feels like a 'flip'. anyone else seeing this?
Samir P: hmm. could be sampling mix or a change in which samples we include when merging routes. did we switch merge-mode or sampling origin?
Micah: what view are you looking at? per-model rollup or the top-level endpoint?
Lina M: top-level endpoint rollup (All regions) -> Metrics / Latency -> p50/p95/p99. clicking into the route breakdown shows each route p50 ~higher than the rollup p50.
Anya C: that sounds like an aggregation artifact. maybe some low-latency cohort got included only in the rollup (cache hits / prefix cached responses).
Lina M: possible — we did push a small KV cache change yesterday morning. deploy-bot says: deploy ops-service@v2.14.3 at 08:14 :rocket:
ops-bot: deploy finished: ops-service v2.14.3 — note: kv-prefix-cache: enable-fast-path=true
Samir P: ok that aligns. if a small high-volume subset is now super-fast, it can drag the rollup p50 down while per-route medians (tagged by route) remain higher because the fast cohort is tagged differently (e.g., cache_hit=true).
Micah: can you share the query/filter you used on the dashboard? paste the raw expression.
Lina M: here — the rollup panel uses the UI default: aggregate( lat_ms, quantiles=[0.5,0.95,0.99], by=[endpoint]) and the route breakdown uses by=[endpoint,route].
Samir P: that still could do it if the rollup collapse ignores the cache_hit tag but the route breakdown includes it. is the rollup sampling origin set to "merged" vs "source"?
Anya C: we recently added a toggle to prefer sample-origin=client for per-route but rollup uses server-origin. two different sample pools is the most likely cause.
Ashok: quick adhoc to confirm: run a grouped quantile by cache_hit. something like:
```
SELECT quantile(0.5)(lat_ms) as p50, count() as n
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY cache_hit
```
Micah: or even a small cohort slice: quantile(0.5) over client_tier='mobile' vs 'web' to see if client mix changed.
Lina M: ran the cache_hit split — results: p50(cache_hit=true)=38ms (n=86k), p50(cache_hit=false)=145ms (n=12k). overall rollup p50=45ms. so large number of cache hits pulled the rollup median down.
Samir P: that matches the hypothesis. route breakdown must be scoped to route-tagged samples where cache_hit isn't applied or has different sampling weight.
Anya C: UX follow-up: the dashboard needs a clear note on sample origin and an option to show "origin-aware" percentiles (i.e., show weighted/unioned percentile or show the sample origin breakdown). current labels are ambiguous.
Ashok: operationally we can: 1) add a small badge on rollups: "sample origin: server (cache hits included)"; 2) add a toggle to compute percentiles only over a chosen origin; 3) expose cohort-split quick links (cache_hit, client_tier, canary=true).
Micah: I can prototype a toggle that switches between "merged/union" vs "origin-specific" percentiles in the panel. low risk change.
Lina M: thanks — action items: Micah to prototype toggle + small UX hint (ETA EOD), Samir to validate that merge-mode doesn't drop tags unintentionally (ETA tomorrow), Anya to draft dashboard copy that explains sample origin (ETA tomorrow), I'll add an eval that asserts rollup vs breakdown on known cohorts.
Samir P: also worth adding a small test: synthetic requests with cache_hit=true heavy volume should not cause percentiles to mislead by default — document expected behavior.
Anya C: agreed. adding doc blurb to the rollout checklist so product owners know when to expect shifts if they enable caches or client sampling changes.
Lina M: awesome. good to close — this was not a bug in quantile code, more a sample-origin/aggregation expectation mismatch. :white_check_mark:
